All 12 tests pass, and I already verified the server boots and behaves correctly via live curl requests.

## Summary

Added `POST /orders` to the catalog-service, following the codebase's existing conventions:

- **`src/data/orderRepository.js`** — in-memory store (same pattern as `productRepository.js`) with `insertIfAbsent(key, data)`. It looks up the idempotency key and inserts synchronously with no `await` in between, so concurrent retries in Node's single-threaded event loop can't race past each other — verified with 5 simultaneous identical requests in the test suite, exactly one order was created.
- **`src/validation/orderValidation.js`** — pure, synchronous validator: requires `idempotencyKey`, a valid `customerEmail`, and a non-empty `items` array where each item has a non-empty `sku` and a positive-integer `quantity`. Returns an error list rather than throwing.
- **`src/routes/orders.js`** — the route: validates shape, then confirms every `sku` exists in the product catalog (via `productRepository.findBySku`), then calls `insertIfAbsent`. Logs a structured JSON line for every attempt (`received`, `rejected`, `created`, or `duplicate_replayed`) with a `requestId` and the client's `idempotencyKey`, so retries are traceable in logs.
- **`src/server.js`** — mounted the new route, added a JSON body-parse error handler (malformed JSON previously fell through to Express's default HTML error page), and exported `app` with `listen` guarded behind `require.main === module` so tests can drive it over real HTTP without binding a port at import time.
- **`src/routes/orders.test.js`** — 12 tests using Node's built-in test runner (no new dependency): validation edge cases, malformed JSON, unknown SKU rejection, single creation, sequential retry (including a retry with different item quantities — the original order wins), 5-way concurrent retry, and distinct keys producing distinct orders. All pass.
